ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60–80 cm. It is dark brown to black with a pale yellow belly and a distinct, light-colored collar behind the head. It features smooth scales and a blunt, rounded snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ferania sieboldii* is best distinguished by its strongly keeled scales and a distinctively broad, flattened head that is clearly demarcated from the neck.
ai.habitat: Siebold's Mud Snake inhabits freshwater wetlands, marshes, and rice paddies in the Indian subcontinent, typically found in low-lying, vegetated areas at low altitudes.
ai.behavior: *Ferania sieboldii* is a nocturnal predator that primarily hunts fish and amphibians by ambushing them in shallow, muddy waters.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ferania sieboldii* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically resulting in litters of 6 to 12 offspring.
ai.distributionRemarks: Ferania sieboldii is found in the coastal regions of India, primarily across West Bengal and Odisha, typically inhabiting low-elevation freshwater and estuarine habitats.
